To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a list of learning outcomes for undergraduate health students, that are required for using electronic patient records in a digital healthcare setting.
the six domains of competence are: 1) digital health, 2) accessing data, 3) communication, 4) generating data, 5) multidisciplinary working, and 6) monitoring and audit.
we developed and defined domains of competence and learning outcomes needed by health graduates to commence working with electronic patient records (EPRs).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a set of competencies and associated learning outcomes for healthcare students to enable them to work with and alongside Electronic Patient Records (ERPs).
the use of EPRs by undergraduate students in healthcare programmes and how they can be integrated into the curriculum.
defining the knowledge, skills, attitudes and values required by healthcare professionals to work with and alongside the digital healthcare environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the six domains of competence can be used to inform the design of undergraduate healthcare programmes and the development of EPRs to ensure that healthcare professionals can work in a digital healthcare system.
these domains of competence and learning outcomes will be used to guide the integration and implementation of EPRs across undergraduate education in the healthcare workforce.

the six domains of competence are: 1) Work as a practitioner in digital healthcare environment, 2) Access and interpret data to inform clinical decisions, 3) Communicate effectively with patients and healthcare professionals, 4) Generate data for and about a patient within the EPR, 5) Work with other healthcare professionals with and along side EPRs and 6) Monitor and improve the quality of care.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the domains and outcomes provide the basis for a curriculum for undergraduate healthcare students in the digital healthcare era.
we have defined six domains of competence for healthcare students to be able to use EPRs in a healthcare environment, and associated learning outcomes for each domain.

we have developed a consensus framework for undergraduate healthcare education that can be used by healthcare educators, healthcare providers and EPR providers to guide the integration and implementation of EPRs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
EPRs are an important part of the healthcare environment and healthcare students should be exposed to EPRs in their undergraduate training.
EPRs are not just a technical tool to be used in healthcare, but rather they should be considered as a core component of the curriculum for undergraduate healthcare programmes.
the domains and outcomes can be used to guide curriculum development and integration of EPR use into undergraduate healthcare programmes.
